items.title: Hybrid mimetic finite-volume diffusion on general meshes
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. For $f\in L^1(\Omega)$, the **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

For an affine function $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, its cell and face averages satisfy $G_K\ell=b$ and $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=0$ by the displayed face-moment closure. The drawing illustrates the cell and face degrees of freedom on a skew cell; no center-to-face orthogonality is assumed.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (3,1) -- (1,1) -- cycle;
  \fill (1.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_K$};
  \fill (1,0) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_{F_1}$};
  \fill (2.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[right] {$u_{F_2}$};
  \fill (2,1) circle (2pt) node[above] {$u_{F_3}$};
  \fill (0.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$u_{F_4}$};
  \draw[->,blue] (1.5,0.5) -- (2.2,0.5) node[right] {$G_Ku$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

When $p=2$, $b_K(\xi)=A_K\xi$, and $\alpha_{0,K}=\lambda_{\min}(A_K)$, the nonlinear formula agrees with the linear form above. Neither specification by itself proves solvability, a conforming $W_0^{1,p}$ reconstruction, or a mesh-uniform discrete Aubin–Lions estimate; those require separate results or hypotheses.
items.strategy: Define cell and face averages, the divergence-based cell gradient, its affine residual, a positive local stabilization, the global hybrid balance, and the optional monotone p-growth evolution form.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used in the finite-dimensional method definition.

items.title: Finite-volume families with a regular simplicial companion

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain, $d\ge1$. A **regular simplicial companion family** consists of refining uniformly regular boundary-anchored cell-face meshes in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], and, for each mesh, a matching simplicial subdivision $\mathcal S_h$ of its cell closures with the following finite geometric data and uniform constants $c,C,J>0$.

Each cell closure $\overline K$ is the union of at most $J$ closed nondegenerate $d$-simplices with pairwise disjoint interiors. Each simplex has diameter at most $Ch$ and inradius at least $ch$, and the chosen cell point $x_K$ is a subdivision vertex. The subdivision of each cell closure is a fan from $x_K$ over a triangulation of its boundary, and subdivisions agree on shared faces. Each original face closure $\overline F$ is a union of at most $J$ closed subdivision facets. In dimension one these mean the two subintervals from $x_K$ to the endpoints.

For each subdivision vertex $z$, let $\mathcal K(z)$ consist of the original cells whose closures contain $z$. This set has at most $J$ elements. For any $K,L\in\mathcal K(z)$ there is a path of at most $J$ cells in $\mathcal K(z)$, from $K$ to $L$, consecutive cells sharing an original face whose closure contains $z$. If $z\in\partial\Omega$, every $K\in\mathcal K(z)$ has such a path to a cell with a boundary face whose closure contains $z$. These are connectivity checks on finite vertex stars, not an assumption of an analytic inequality.

For shared face values $v_F$, cell values $v_K$, and homogeneous boundary values $v_F=0$, define the piecewise constant state $\Pi_hv|_K=v_K$ and
$$D_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|v_F-v_K|^p\qquad(1<p<\infty).$$
The mean interpolator $I_hv$ has cell and face values equal to the corresponding means of a Sobolev function, with face means interpreted by the simplex trace; for $v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ its boundary face means are zero. Define $E_hv$ to be continuous and affine on each subdivision simplex, with nodal value $|\mathcal K(z)|^{-1}\sum_{K\in\mathcal K(z)}v_K$ at an interior vertex $z$ and zero at a boundary vertex. Thus $E_h$ is an explicit linear function of the cell values; its definition does not assume its stability.

These conditions allow nonorthogonal cells. A nonempty example in every dimension is the uniform cubical partition of $(0,1)^d$, with cell centers, a fixed matching barycentric subdivision of every face, and the cones from cell centers to those face simplices. Scaling leaves finitely many simplex shapes and bounded vertex stars; coordinate adjacency connects each interior star and connects each boundary star to a boundary face. In dimension one use equal subintervals and their midpoints. Hence all the displayed constants can be chosen independently of refinement.

items.title: TPFA discrete Green identity, coercivity, and maximum principle
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite TPFA-admissible cell-face mesh, let every cell be connected through interior faces to a cell with a boundary face, and let $T_F>0$ be the transmissibilities of [[def-tpfa-harmonic-face-scheme]]. For cell vectors $u,v$, define
$$ (A_hu)_K=\frac1{|K|}\left(\sum_{F=K|L}T_F(u_K-u_L)+\sum_{F\subset\partial K\cap\partial\Omega}T_{K,F}u_K\right). $$
Then interior fluxes are locally conservative, and for all cell vectors $u,v$,
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|v_K(A_hu)_K= \sum_{F=K|L\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}T_F(v_K-v_L)(u_K-u_L) +\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}T_{K,F}v_Ku_K. $$
The stiffness matrix associated with the displayed bilinear identity is symmetric positive definite. Equivalently, $A_h$ is self-adjoint and positive definite in the volume-weighted inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_h=\sum_K|K|u_Kv_K$; its ordinary coordinate matrix need not be symmetric when cell volumes differ. Hence every finite source and boundary-data vector gives a unique solution. If all cell sources and all prescribed boundary face values are nonnegative, then every solution cell value is nonnegative. The maximum-principle claim uses the boundary anchor; no diagonal sign statement alone is used as a substitute for that condition.
items.strategy: Pair the cell balance with a test vector, collect the two signed contributions at each interior face, and use positivity plus boundary anchoring for injectivity and the minimum argument.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the graph and all sums are finite.

items.title: Discrete Poincaré inequality from boundary paths
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite boundary-anchored TPFA mesh and let $T_e>0$ be its interior and boundary transmissibilities. A **boundary path family** assigns to each cell $K$ a finite simple path $\gamma_K$ of adjacent interior faces, followed by one boundary face of its terminal cell; simple means it visits no cell more than once. Set $\Delta_eu=u_K-u_L$ on an interior face $e=K|L$ with a fixed orientation, and set $\Delta_eu=u_K$ on a boundary face of $K$. The sign of an interior increment is reversed when the path traverses the fixed orientation backward. Put
$$ S_K=\sum_{e\in\gamma_K}T_e^{-1},\qquad C_{\rm path}=\max_{e}\sum_{K:e\in\gamma_K}|K|S_K. $$
Then every cell vector $u$ satisfies the discrete Poincaré inequality
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|u_K^2\le C_{\rm path}\sum_{e}T_e(\Delta_eu)^2=C_{\rm path}\|u\|_{E_h}^2. $$
Consequently, any uniformly regular mesh family supplied with boundary path families whose $C_{\rm path}$ are uniformly bounded has a mesh-uniform Poincaré constant. This theorem does not assert that every orthogonal mesh family has such a uniform path bound.
items.strategy: Write each cell value as the signed sum of its path increments, apply weighted Cauchy–Schwarz, and exchange the finite cell-edge sums using the stated congestion bound.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the paths are finite data and all sums are finite.

items.title: Coercivity, monotonicity, conservation, and affine exactness of the mimetic schemes
items.statement:
Let a finite boundary-anchored cell-face mesh satisfy the face-moment closure in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]], and let every $A_K$ be symmetric positive definite. Define the local seminorm
$$ \|v\|_{K,\mathrm{mim}}^2=|K||G_Kv|^2+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(v)^2. $$
Its kernel consists exactly of the constant local vectors $v_K=v_F=c$, so it induces a norm modulo constants. Then $\mathscr A_K(v,v)\ge\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\|v\|_{K,\mathrm{mim}}^2$. The global Dirichlet matrix of the linear hybrid mimetic scheme is symmetric positive definite and has a unique solution for every finite cell-source vector. Its induced numerical fluxes satisfy the cellwise balance and opposite-flux identity on each interior face. For any affine $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, the local linear flux is exactly $Q_{K,F}(\ell)=-|F|(A_Kb)\cdot n_{K,F}$. For the nonlinear $p$-growth extension in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]], the spatial operator is monotone and coercive in the reconstructed gradient and residual variables, and its shared interior face fluxes are conservative at each implicit time step.
items.strategy: Use the divergence theorem to prove affine gradient reproduction, then use the residual stabilization and constant-vector kernel to prove coercivity, global uniqueness, and face balance.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; all spaces are finite-dimensional.

items.title: Finite-volume companions, mean tests and weak-gradient closure

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and a family in [[def-fv-regular-simplicial-companion-family]]. For $1<p<\infty$ and zero boundary face values, put
$$B_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K|K||G_Kv|^p+S_{h,p}(v)^p,\qquad S_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_{K,F}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(v)|^p,$$
where $G_K,\rho_{K,F}$ have the formulas in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]]. Then, with constants independent of $h,v$,
$$C^{-1}D_{h,p}(v)\le B_{h,p}(v)\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|E_hv\|_{W^{1,p}}\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_{L^p}\le ChD_{h,p}(v).$$
Here $E_hv\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. If $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$ and $\vartheta=1-d\max(1/p-1/2,0)>0$, also
$$\|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_2\le Ch^\vartheta D_{h,p}(v),\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_2+\|\Pi_hv\|_p\le CD_{h,p}(v).$$
For $z\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, $D_{h,p}(I_hz)\le C\|\nabla z\|_p$. If the cell points are volume centroids, then for smooth $z$ with compact support in $\Omega$, $G_h I_hz\to\nabla z$ uniformly and $S_{h,p}(I_hz)\le Ch\|D^2z\|_\infty$, where $G_hv|_K=G_Kv$. Finally, for every smooth vector field $\phi$ on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$,
$$\left|\int_\Omega G_hv\cdot\phi+\Pi_hv\,\operatorname{div}\phi\right|\le ChD_{h,p}(v)\|\nabla\phi\|_\infty.$$
Consequently bounded $D_{h,p}(v_h)$, strong $L^p$ convergence $\Pi_hv_h\to v$, and weak $L^p$ convergence $G_hv_h\rightharpoonup g$ imply $g=\nabla v$ distributionally. The same statements hold after integration in time with the corresponding $L^p$ bounds.

items.title: TPFA flux-energy convergence for smooth face-aligned interfaces
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded connected polyhedral set and let $(\mathcal T_h)$ be a refining, uniformly regular, boundary-anchored family of TPFA-admissible meshes. Assume $\lambda_K\in[\lambda_*,\lambda^*]$ with $0<\lambda_*\le\lambda^*<\infty$, constant on each cell, and that coefficient jumps occur only across mesh faces. Suppose $u$ is continuous, vanishes on $\partial\Omega$, and is $C^2$ on each cell closure with the uniform family bound
$$ M=\sup_h\max_{K\in\mathcal K_h}\|D^2u\|_{L^\infty(K)}<\infty. $$
For every interior face $F=K|L$ fix an orientation and define its exact outward flux from $K$ by $J_{K,F}=-\int_F\lambda_K\nabla u|_K\cdot n_{K,F}$. On a boundary face define $J_{K,F}$ by the same formula. Assume the exact fluxes satisfy the cell balances $\sum_{F\subset\partial K}J_{K,F}=\int_K f$ and $J_{K,F}=-J_{L,F}$ on every interior face. Let $U_h$ solve the TPFA cell balances with source $f$ and zero boundary values, and let $I_hu$ be the cell-center sample $u(x_K)$ with zero boundary face values. Then, for a constant $C$ depending only on $\Omega$, $\lambda_*,\lambda^*$, and the uniform mesh regularity bounds,
$$ \|U_h-I_hu\|_{E_h}\le C hM,\qquad \left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}\frac{|Q_{K,F}(U_h)-J_{K,F}|^2}{T_F}+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}\frac{|Q_{K,F}(U_h)-J_{K,F}|^2}{T_{K,F}}\right)^{1/2}\le 2ChM. $$
The second estimate is convergence of the reconstructed numerical face flux in the transmissibility-dual energy norm. No pointwise operator consistency on arbitrary nonorthogonal meshes or error rate for nonsmooth weak solutions is asserted.
items.strategy: Use the common face-average exact flux, bound each cell normal trace deviation by the Hessian bound, and use normal Taylor expansion and conservative energy testing.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite sums and Taylor's theorem.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let TPFA-admissible meshes also form a regular simplicial companion family, with homogeneous Dirichlet data and fixed $0<\lambda_*\le\lambda_K\le\lambda^*$. If cell vectors $v_h$ satisfy $\sup_h\|v_h\|_{E_h}<\infty$, there are a subsequence and $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ such that $\Pi_hv_h\to v$ strongly in $L^2(\Omega)$, and the gradients of the conforming companions converge weakly to $\nabla v$ in $L^2$.

There is also an explicit physical weak-gradient reconstruction. Let $P_{K,F}$ be the pyramid with vertex $x_K$ and base $\overline F$, ignoring its measure-zero boundary. For $F=K|L$ put $\mathcal D_F=P_{K,F}\cup P_{L,F}$, fix the normal $n=n_{K,F}$, and define
$$\mathcal G_hv=d\frac{v_L-v_K}{d_F}n\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D_F.$$
On a boundary pyramid put $\mathcal G_hv=-dv_Kn_{K,F}/d_{K,F}$. These regions partition $\Omega$ up to null sets. Along the same subsequence $\mathcal G_hv_h\rightharpoonup\nabla v$ in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\|\mathcal G_hv_h\|_2^2=d\left(\sum_{F=K|L}\frac{|F|}{d_F}|v_L-v_K|^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}|v_K|^2\right)\le\frac d{\lambda_*}\|v_h\|_{E_h}^2.$$
The dimension factor $d$ is essential. This physical gradient differs from the face-copy bookkeeping gradient in the TPFA Definition; no identification of that separate copy space with $\Omega$ is asserted.

items.title: Conditional monotone finite-volume parabolic limit identification
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, put $p'=p/(p-1)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ for $T>0$. Let $a(x,\xi)$ satisfy the Carathéodory, $p$-growth, coercivity, and monotonicity hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]].

For each $m$, let $\mathcal P_m$ be a finite measurable partition of $\Omega$ into cells of positive measure and let a finite time partition carry cell values. Let $\bar U_m$ be the function constant on each resulting space-time cell. Suppose there are conforming reconstructions $w_m\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and a function $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$ \bar U_m\to u\text{ strongly in }L^p(0,T;H),\qquad \|\bar U_m-w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;H)}\to0, $$
and $\sup_m\|w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;V)}<\infty$. Write $\xi_m=\nabla w_m$ and $q_m=a(x,\xi_m)$. Assume, along the same subsequence, $q_m\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$ and
$$ \limsup_{m\to\infty}\int_Qq_m\cdot\xi_m\le\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u. $$
Finally, assume $f\in L^{p'}(Q)$, $u_0\in H$, and the finite-volume weak identities have residuals $r_m(\varphi)\to0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$:
$$ -\int_Q\bar U_m\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq_m\cdot\nabla\varphi-\int_Qf\varphi-\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx=r_m(\varphi). $$
Then $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere, and $u$ is a weak evolution solution of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$ with initial trace $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]:
$$ -\int_Q u\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_Qf\varphi+\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx $$
for every such test function. This is a conditional finite-volume limit-identification result; the reconstruction, residual, compactness, and energy hypotheses are not conclusions of the statement.
items.strategy: Apply PE12 weak compactness to the assumed conforming reconstructions, pass the discrete weak identity under the stated residual hypothesis, and apply Minty's lemma using the discrete energy limsup.
items.axiom_base: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It is used only by the PE12 weak-gradient compactness and Minty supplier chain; no additional choice is used in the finite-volume balance passage.

items.title: Energy and computed-state compactness for hybrid mimetic backward Euler

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let hybrid meshes in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]] form a regular simplicial companion family, with cell points equal to volume centroids, and let $0<\underline\alpha\le\alpha_{0,K}\le\overline\alpha<\infty$ uniformly. Let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a$ have precisely the Carathéodory, growth, coercivity and monotonicity hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. Let $f\in L^{p'}(Q)$, $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$, and let initial cell states obey $\Pi_hU_h^0\to u_0$ strongly in $H=L^2(\Omega)$. Each finite backward-Euler step in the hybrid Definition has a solution. Initial face values can be set arbitrarily because only initial cell values occur in the time term.

On arbitrary time partitions with maximum step $\delta_h\to0$, every selection of step solutions satisfies, uniformly in $h$,
$$\max_n\|\Pi_hU_h^n\|_2^2+\sum_n\|\Pi_h(U_h^n-U_h^{n-1})\|_2^2+\sum_n\tau_n B_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\le C.$$
Here $B_{h,p},D_{h,p},S_{h,p},G_h$ are as in [[lem-fv-conforming-companion-and-test-recovery]]. Extend $\overline U_h$ by $U_h^n$ on $(t_{n-1},t_n]$. The piecewise affine interpolation of $\Pi_hU_h^n$ has derivative bounded in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. There are a subsequence and $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$\Pi_h\overline U_h\to u\text{ in }L^r(0,T;H)\ (1\le r<\infty)\text{ and in }L^p(Q),$$
$$E_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),\qquad G_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup\nabla u\text{ in }L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d).$$
No mesh/time coupling or time-step ratio restriction is required.

items.title: Computed hybrid mimetic states and numerical fluxes converge to monotone diffusion

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Under exactly the hypotheses of [[lem-hybrid-mimetic-backward-euler-energy-and-compactness]], the computed cell states converge, along a subsequence, to a weak evolution solution $u$ of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$, $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. In addition to the strong state convergences in that lemma, the actual constitutive fields
$$q_h(t,x)=a(x,G_KU_h^n)\quad(t\in(t_{n-1},t_n],\ x\in K)$$
converge weakly in $L^{p'}(Q)$ to $a(x,\nabla u)$, and
$$\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\longrightarrow\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \sum_n\tau_n S_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\longrightarrow0.$$
The final cell states converge strongly to $u(T)$ in $H$.

This includes convergence of a physical reconstruction of the actual numerical face fluxes. Let $r_{K,F}=x_F-x_K$, $s_{K,F}^n=\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n))$, $b_K^n=b_K(G_KU_h^n)$, and $c_K^n=|K|^{-1}\sum_Fs_{K,F}^nr_{K,F}$. On the physical pyramid $P_{K,F}$ with vertex $x_K$ and base $\overline F$ set
$$q_h^{\rm num}=b_K^n-c_K^n+\frac{s_{K,F}^n}{|F|}n_{K,F}.$$
Then $-|F|q_h^{\rm num}|_{P_{K,F}}\cdot n_{K,F}=Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(U_h^n)$ exactly, $q_h^{\rm num}-b_h\to0$ strongly in $L^{p'}(Q)$, with $b_h|_K=b_K^n$, and $q_h^{\rm num}\rightharpoonup a(x,\nabla u)$ in $L^{p'}(Q)$. No strong convergence of $G_h\overline U_h$ is inferred from mere monotonicity.

Finally the hypotheses of [[lem-mimetic-fv-parabolic-limit-identification]] can be supplied on this same subsequence by conforming limit recovery: take $w_h=u$ and $\widetilde q_h=a(x,\nabla w_h)=a(x,\nabla u)$. These are post-limit conforming functions, distinct from the computed companions $E_h\overline U_h$, constitutive fields $q_h$, and numerical fluxes $q_h^{\rm num}$. The computed convergence assertion above is established independently of this recovery observation.

title: Finite-volume diffusion on admissible meshes — Examples

items.title: Harmonic TPFA flux on a rectangular Voronoï mesh
items.statement: Take $\Omega=(0,2)\times(0,1)$ and the two rectangular cells $K=(0,1)\times(0,1)$ and $L=(1,2)\times(0,1)$. Their centers are $(1/2,1/2)$ and $(3/2,1/2)$, so the shared vertical face is orthogonal to the center segment. Set $\lambda_K=\lambda_L=1$, use $u(x,y)=x$, and impose its exact face-center values on the six cell faces on the outer boundary. The exact source is $f=0$.
items.strategy: Compute cell and face centers, transmissibilities, and signed fluxes directly from the TPFA definition.

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, Vol. VII, 2000; complete updated author text
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.2, Example 9.2, printed pp. 39–40: Voronoï meshes and orthogonality.

items.title: A nonorthogonal two-point flux gives a false transverse flux
items.statement: The Euclidean two-point flux formula $Q_{K,F}=|F|(u_K-u_L)/|x_L-x_K|$ is consistent for isotropic diffusion on every cell-face mesh, including nonorthogonal meshes.
items.strategy: Give two explicit triangles sharing a vertical face and evaluate the naive two-point formula on u(x,y)=y.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: §2.3–§3, PDF pp. 10–16: TPFA's orthogonality limitation and the need for multipoint methods on general meshes.

items.title: Harmonic transmissibility across a one-dimensional material interface
items.statement: Let $\Omega=(0,1)$ with cells $K=(0,1/2)$ and $L=(1/2,1)$, chosen centers $x_K=1/4$ and $x_L=3/4$, cell coefficients $\lambda_K=1$ and $\lambda_L=9$, and boundary values $u(0)=0$, $u(1)=1$. The stationary continuous solution has constant flux across the material interface. Compare the TPFA transmissibility using the two half-cell resistances with the transmissibility obtained by substituting the arithmetic coefficient mean.
items.strategy: Solve the two-resistance continuous problem exactly and compare its interface flux with harmonic and arithmetic TPFA transmissibilities.

references.locator: Chapter 7 §7.2 and Chapter 11 §11.1, printed pp. 22–24 and 78–81: discontinuous diffusion and resistance-weighted harmonic transmissibility.

items.title: Affine anisotropic flux on a skew parallelogram
items.statement: Take the single parallelogram cell with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(3,1),(1,1)$, tensor $A=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$, and affine state $u(x,y)=x+2y$. Prescribe on each boundary face its exact face mean. The cell center is $(3/2,1/2)$ and the face centers, in bottom/right/top/left order, are $(1,0),(5/2,1/2),(2,1),(1/2,1/2)$. This cell is skew: its right and left face normals are not parallel to the vectors from the cell center to those face centers.
items.strategy: Evaluate the face means and integrated outward normals, then verify the reconstructed gradient and tensor-weighted fluxes.
